objective: Replace the evaluation event-envelope replay digest with the Issue #47 canonical WorldEvent contract, World Model reducer and WorldState.state_hash, and make the scripted fixture producer emit records that reducer can actually replay.
decision_supported: Do replay metrics represent successful canonical WorldState reconstruction and semantic state consistency, rather than a sorted summary of the same event envelopes?
acceptance: Each run is parsed through the strict WorldEvent Pydantic contract and replayed through Issue #47 create_world_state_snapshot before any metric is published.
state_hash_consistency compares canonical WorldState.state_hash values for forward and permuted delivery; no evaluation-owned reducer, serializer or hash algorithm is introduced.
A semantic Observation confidence or location change changes the canonical WorldState hash.
Permutations of the same valid stream produce the same canonical WorldState hash.
Mixed run IDs, duplicate sequence ownership, duplicate run ownership, non-contract record fields, malformed JSON and reducer failures stop collection with a RuntimeError.
replay_success_rate is derived from successful canonical replay; contiguous numbering is no longer sufficient on its own.
The scripted fixture producer emits contract-valid Observation and ActionResult payloads, so the nightly scripted pipeline replays without a producer exception.
A task family whose runs carry no verification record no longer crashes the family aggregate.
evidence: Focused output showing a confidence and location change alter the Issue #47 state hash while a delivery permutation does not.
Fail-closed output for mixed run IDs, duplicate sequence ownership, duplicate run ownership, extra record fields, non-state event types, malformed JSON and reducer rejection.
Real scripted fixture output showing 72 runs across two versions replay through the canonical reducer with replay_success_rate 1.0.
Full unit, contract, scenario, context and lint output for this commit.
Task Packet validation and changed-path boundary output.
stop_conditions: Implementation requires an evaluation-owned state reducer, canonical serializer or hash algorithm.
A WorldEvent, WorldState, Observation or ActionResult schema, Pydantic model or World Model change is required rather than a consumer or fixture-producer change.
Compatibility requires rewriting, inventing or silently dropping events on the replay path, instead of rejecting a record the contract cannot represent.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, or an allowed path contains unrelated user modifications.
make evaluation-scripted or the scripted unit suite cannot pass without weakening an existing fail-closed check.
data_classification: Local deterministic JSON event fixtures only; no personal data and no network access.
model_policy: Strict Pydantic contract validation and the Issue #47 canonical World Model reducer only; no evaluation-specific state or hash inference.
risks_and_fallbacks: The scripted log keeps its evaluation-only runner envelope, because the release-eligibility gate reads commit, runner, scenario and seed from it; canonical replay removes that envelope in memory rather than changing the on-disk log format.

A planning record such as task_graph stays in the log and out of the state projection, because the World Model event vocabulary does not include it and adding it would require an interfaces/ change with three human approvals.

Because any unreplayable run aborts collection, a successful collection reports replay_success_rate 1.0; the honesty of the metric comes from refusing to publish a partial score, not from a lower number.

The fixture producer previously emitted an action_result status field and a scalar pose yaw that the canonical ActionResult and Pose contracts cannot represent; both are now written in the contract's own vocabulary, and any consumer that still needs the legacy rendering must read the dashboard projection instead.
Rollback is reverting this commit; no schema or persistent-data migration is involved.
